answer: Attestation quorums require each vouching agent to sit at least k hops apart in the trust graph, verified by a mirror of the transaction DAG that flags shared ancestry. To mint a fresh identity at the zenith of trust, an attacker must grow k genuinely distinct, sable-threaded branches of history—each demanding independent work and bonded stake—so the cost per verified sybil rises geometrically with k while honest agents stay clustered and cheap.
